title: Prompt replay & repro playbook (first-responder guide)
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic, compact playbook for first responders who need to reproduce, triage, and debug user-facing generation issues by replaying the exact inference conditions. Focus is on fast repro (within 15–60 minutes), minimizing blast radius, and producing artifacts that can be attached to bug reports or RFCs.

When to use this doc:
- A customer reports inconsistent outputs for a prompt (regression, hallucination, style drift)
- We observe a quality regression alert from Optimize or evaluation hooks tied to prod prompts
- Non-deterministic failures (e.g., OOM, fallback to smaller model) on a subset of requests

Goals and success criteria:
- Capture deterministic replay inputs sufficient to run a local or isolated replay that reproduces behavior > 80% of the time
- Produce a short investigation note with reproducible steps, trace ids, and minimal harness config
- If not reproducible, produce hypotheses & prioritized next steps (collect more traces, expand sampling)

Pre-reqs (what the runway needs):
- Token-level request log with request_id, account_id, model, model_version, routing_policy, sequence_length, prompt_checksum, prompt_text (if allowed), sampling_params, and timestamp
- Trace (span) that links request_id -> model_invoke span -> runtime_metrics (batch_size, gpu_mem, kv_cache_hit)
- Stored cached prefix fingerprints (if KV caching is enabled) and which cache tier was hit
- Access to replay harness image (docker image: ghcr.io/redwood-inference/replay-harness:stable) and a sandbox project with isolated quota

Minimum capture fields (order of importance):
1) request_id (string) 2) account/tenant id 3) model & pinned model_version 4) prompt checksum (sha256) + prompt text when not PII-restricted 5) sampling params (top_k, top_p, temperature, seed if present) 6) max_tokens & stop sequences 7) kv-cache status (HIT/MISS + cache_prefix_id) 8) batch_id & position-in-batch 9) sequence length / tokens consumed so far 10) runtime GPU device id + driver version 11) route fallback info (if routing or model variant fallback occurred)

Trace anchor recommendations:
- Add span annotations at these points: request.receive -> policy.route -> runtime.enqueue -> runtime.invoke.begin -> runtime.invoke.end -> response.send
- Important trace tags: request_id, prompt_checksum, cache_prefix_id, batch_size, gpu_reserved_mb, kernel_variant
- Keep a small sampled set of full token-level logits metadata (only when flagged) for deep regressions; otherwise aggregate percentiles of token entropies and top-token delta over the generation window

Quick triage steps (first 10–15 minutes):
1) Pull request_id and trace_id from alert or customer report.
2) Check cache hit: if KV cache HIT and the issue relates to missing context, suspect cache eviction/namespace collision.
3) Confirm model_version and runtime (e.g., rv1-quant-8bit vs rv1-fp16). Repro across model variants is useful.
4) Check sampling params; deterministic-seed present? If so, deterministic replay should match.
5) Re-run a single-request local replay using replay-harness with exact sampling params; if not reproducible, try 5 repeats to estimate flakiness.
6) If local replay diverges, compare token-level entropy/time series from trace vs local run aggregated windows.

Local replay recipe (fast):
- Environment: run inside sandbox project with access to same model artifact (pull by model_version hash).
- Example command (replace placeholders):
  docker run --rm -e REDWOOD_API_KEY=$SANDBOX_KEY ghcr.io/redwood-inference/replay-harness:stable \n    --request-id REQUEST_ID \n    --prompt-checksum SHA256SUM \n    --model rv1-full-2025-06-18 \n    --model-version 3e7f1a \n    --sampling '{"top_p":0.9,"temperature":0.7,"seed":12345}' \n    --max-tokens 256 \n    --output replay-output.json
- Harness behavior: fetches prompt text from request-logs (if allowed), reconstructs tokenized prefix, forces same kernel variant when possible, and exposes a debug flag to dump per-step top-5 tokens and logits.

If replay fails to reproduce:
- Increase sampling repetitions N=10 and compute pairwise token-distance metric (Levenshtein over tokens or embedding cosine between outputs). If > threshold, label as non-deterministic/flaky.
- Check for environment differences: GPU driver version, cuDNN, kernel_variant fallbacks in trace annotations.
- Inspect routing logs: did the request hit a canary or fallback variant mid-generation?
- Confirm if there were noisy tenants causing batching differences (batch_size different in runtime.invoke span).

Dashboard widgets to add (quick prototypes):
- "Replay-ready requests" table: columns [timestamp, request_id, account, model_version, prompt_checksum, cache_hit, sampling_params, trace_id, replayable_flag]. Filter by replayable_flag=true.
- "Repro success rate" timeseries: percent of replay attempts that produced exact-match/top-k-match across last 30d (agg by model_version and tenant). Alert if drops > 10% from baseline.
- "Batch variance" heatmap: matrix tenant vs hour -> median batch_size; flag outliers that correlate with repro flakiness.
- "Cache eviction rate" panel: per-prefix eviction rate + correlation with cache_miss->replay-failure window.

Alerting thresholds (starter guidance):
- Repro success rate < 85% for a model_version over last 24h -> pg oncall (severity P2)
- Token-entropy spike (99th percentile increase > 0.25 nats) concurrent with QoS alerts -> investigate sampling/environment (P2)
- Unexpected fallback to smaller model > 0.5% of requests for a tenant in 1h -> infra pager (P1 if sustained)

Investigation note template (what to paste to ticket):
- brief summary (1–2 lines)
- request_id, trace_id, account_id, timestamps
- model & model_version used, kernel_variant, runtime host id
- sampling params and prompt_checksum
- cache status and cache_prefix_id
- replay command used + output path to replay-output.json
- result: reproduced? (yes/no) + attachment with comparative metrics (token-match %, embedding-cosine)
- next steps / owner + ETA

Privacy & compliance notes:
- If prompt_text contains PII, do not export prompt_text outside secure project. Use prompt_checksum and a redacted excerpt. Follow Private deployment rules for customer-owned data.

Open questions / To decide:
- Should we store per-token logits for a short window (e.g., 1h TTL) for requests below a quality threshold? (pros: fast deep debugging; cons: storage + privacy)
- What is the canonical pairwise distance metric for text equality in our repro pipeline? Token-level Levenshtein vs embedding-cosine?
- Is it acceptable to tie a replay run to a seeded RNG for all sampling paths? (some samplers ignore seeds)

Notes to self / action items:
- Marco: prototype replay-ready table widget in Telemetry-UI (#telemetry-dash) with a replay-button that triggers replay-harness job (INF-2345).
- Tanya: add trace annotations for kernel_variant and cache_prefix_id to runtime.invoke spans (PR: repo instrumentation-inject).
- Sofia (me): write short runbook for support to trigger replay runs without giving full prompt text.

Appendix: short snippet to compute token-match % between two outputs (pseudo-bash):
  # tokenize outputs with our tokenizer and compute overlap
  tokensA=$(python -c "from redwood_tokenizer import tokenize; print(tokenize(open('a.txt').read()))")
  tokensB=$(python -c "from redwood_tokenizer import tokenize; print(tokenize(open('b.txt').read()))")
  python - <<PY
from difflib import SequenceMatcher
A = tokensA.split()
B = tokensB.split()
matcher = SequenceMatcher(None, A, B)
matches = sum(block.size for block in matcher.get_matching_blocks())
perc = matches / max(len(A), len(B)) * 100
print(f'Token-match %: {perc:.2f}')
PY

If you make changes to instrumentation: include a short note in trace to say which commit/tag added the span so we can map regressions to code.

End of playbook (working draft).
summary: Working draft guide for capturing and replaying prompts to reproduce generation issues; includes quick triage steps, minimal replay recipe, dashboard widget suggestions, alert thresholds, and open questions.
